subject: Post-demo: recommended model shortlist & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>

Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 1 Mar 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: recommended model shortlist & next steps

Hi Bethany / Jared 

Thanks again for taking the demo this morning. Quick recap and the model shortlist I promised while the team reviews your eval rubric:

High-level from our call:
- Primary UXC: real-time intelligent summarization + short-answer QA for service tickets (median doc length ~1,200 tokens).
- SLA: 95th%-tile latency under 500ms for user-facing flows, background batch can be slower.
- Cost target: target to be under $0.003/active session on average.
- Data/Compliance: must live in US-only VPC for now.

Attached: acme_benchmark_summary_20270301.csv (end-to-end latency/cost), acme_prompt_set_v1.json (sample prompts we ran). Also uploaded the full benchmark workbook here: https://drive.google.com/acme-post-demo-prompts

Recommended shortlist (tradeoffs summarized):
1) redwood-rlhf-7b (recommended-first)	6 Best latency/cost balance for interactive flows. Good instruction-following on your prompt set; ~220ms median token latency on P4-like infra in our bench, estimated cost ~$0.0018 per session. Quality: high for summarization and short-answer with few-shot prompt.
2) redwood-13b-quant (balanced-quality)	6 Higher quality on edge cases (longer reasoning), ~350ms median token latency, estimated cost ~$0.0026 per session after quantization. Recommend for users where precision matters and budget allows.
3) open-instruct-20b (fallback/high-quality)	6 Best quality on complex multi-step answers but notably higher cost and latency (~700ms median for the flows we measured). Use as a background reranker or as a canary for quality-sensitive batches.

Immediate next steps I recommend:
- Your team picks 1 primary and 1 fallback from above for a 2-week POC.
- We’ll share an updated benchmarking run targeted at your exact infra budget (Rishi + Dev will own).
- Schedule a short sync to lock the rollout plan and SLA expectations	6 propose Wed 3/3 10am PT.

Let me know if you want a tighter cost model for multi-region or burst scenarios.

Best,
Marissa
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai
(415) 555-0142

Thanks Marissa 
 this is helpful. A couple quick clarifying Qs from our side:

1) For redwood-rlhf-7b, can you share what quantization / runtime you used for the numbers in the CSV? We care about 95th%-tile latency rather than median.
2) For the 13b option, is there a straightforward tuning recommendation (prompt-engineering vs small fine-tune) to close the gap on the very short answers we rely on?
3) Compliance: we need KMS + audit log confirmation for the POC  can Rishi confirm?

We’re leaning toward picking the 7b as the default but want a fallback plan for customers who need higher precision. Wed 3/3 10am PT works for the sync.

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>

Cc: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 2 Mar 2027 11:26:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: recommended model shortlist & next steps

Hi Bethany 
 quick answers: 

1) redwood-rlhf-7b benchmarks were run on our P4-equivalent dedicated nodes with int8 quantization and kernel autotuning enabled. Median token lat=~220ms; 95th%-tile on the exact prompt set in the CSV is ~480ms. We can re-run on a 95th%-tile focused workload and post the new CSV.

2) For 13b, we recommend: start with prompt engineering + 2-shot examples (we’ve attached acme_prompt_set_v1.json). If gaps persist on short factual answers, a small adapter-style fine-tune (1–2M tokens) closes most of the gap while keeping cost ~10–12% above quantized runtime.

3) Compliance: confirm we support customer-managed KMS and audit logs for Private/Dedicated deployments. I’ll DM the SOC2 readout and a KMS integration checklist.

Next: Dev and I will prepare a focused 95th%-tile re-run and a cost sensitivity table for your expected 100k monthly sessions. We’ll share by EOD Tue 3/2. Meeting confirmed Wed 3/3 10am PT  invite incoming.

Thanks,
Rishi
VP, Infrastructure  Redwood Inference

Bethany 
 quick technical addendum before the sync: 

- Re-run plan: we’ll execute a 95th%-tile benchmark with your production prompt set (attached) on both a P4 and an A10 profile. Expect separate CSVs: latency + cost per session + token breakdown.
- Latency knobs: we can enable KV prefix caching for repeated ticket templates which should reduce 95th%-tile by ~60–120ms for interactive flows.
- Quantization note: redwood-13b-quant in our tests preserves most summarization quality with 4-bit quant in the 13b path; cost uplift vs 7b-int8 is ~35% but quality delta on edge cases is measurable.
- Quick rollout suggestion: start with redwood-rlhf-7b for UI flows + redwood-13b-quant behind an async reranker for any low-confidence outputs (confidence threshold we can tune during POC).

I’ve attached the prompt set and a small script stub we use to run the POC bench. See attached: acme_prompt_set_v1.json

See you all Wed morning.

 Dev
